verses.text: The Israelites again did what was evil in the LORD's sight, and the LORD handed them over to the Philistines for forty years.
A man named Manoah lived in Zorah and belonged to the tribe of Dan. His wife was unable to have children.
The LORD's angel appeared to her and said, “You've been unable to have children, but you're going to become pregnant and give birth to a son.
Be careful now: don't drink wine or strong drink, and don't eat anything unclean.
You're going to give birth to a son. Never cut his hair, because the boy will be a Nazirite, set apart for God from the womb. He'll begin to rescue Israel from the Philistines.”
The woman went and told her husband, “A man of God came to me. His face looked like the face of God's angel. It was overwhelming. I didn't ask where he came from, and he didn't tell me his name.

But he told me, ‘You're going to become pregnant and give birth to a son. Don't drink wine or strong drink, and don't eat anything unclean. The boy will be a Nazirite, set apart for God from the womb until the day he dies.’”
Manoah prayed to the LORD, “Please, Lord, let the man of God you sent come back and teach us what to do for the boy who will be born.”
God listened to Manoah, and God's angel came back to the woman while she was sitting in the field. Her husband wasn't with her.
She ran to tell her husband, “Look! The man who came to me the other day has appeared again!”
Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he reached the man, he asked, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” He answered, “I am.”
Manoah said, “May what you've said come true. How is the boy to live, and what is he to do?”
The LORD's angel told Manoah, “Your wife must take care to do everything I told her.
She mustn't eat anything from the grapevine, drink wine or strong drink, or eat anything unclean. She must follow everything I commanded her.”
Manoah said to the LORD's angel, “Please stay while we prepare a young goat for you.”
The LORD's angel answered, “Even if I stay, I won't eat your food. If you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” Manoah didn't yet realize he was the LORD's angel.
Manoah asked, “What's your name? We want to honor you when what you've said comes true.”
The LORD's angel answered, “Why do you ask my name? It's beyond what you can understand.”
So Manoah took the young goat and the grain offering and offered them to the LORD on the rock. Then the angel did something amazing while Manoah and his wife watched.
As the flames rose from the altar toward the sky, the LORD's angel rose in the flames. Manoah and his wife saw it and fell facedown to the ground.
The LORD's angel didn't appear to Manoah or his wife again. Then Manoah realized who he was.
Manoah told his wife, “We're sure to die. We've seen God.”
His wife said, “If the LORD had wanted to kill us, he wouldn't have accepted our burnt offering and grain offering. He wouldn't have shown us all these things or told us what he just did.”
The woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson. He grew up, and the LORD blessed him.
The LORD's Spirit began to stir in him at Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
